hypothesis: The residual +40.4 no-source margin is RELATIONAL: distractors written as mutations of the key make the recipe invertible, so a solver reconstructs the withheld utterance from the option set. Removing the recipe should collapse the margin toward the fixed-letter control.
construction: Four FAMILIES of four items. Within a family the four items share ONE option set, and every option is the real key for exactly one of the four stimuli. No option is derived from another; there is no filler. A blind solver therefore cannot do better than chance across a family by construction — any fixed strategy scores exactly 1 of 4 — while every option stays a genuine, tempting reply once the stimulus is heard.
whyNotTheEndpointsAlreadyMeasured: Options from UNRELATED items scored +9.9 no-source but 0% hard with-source (obviously wrong once you hear it). Options as mutations of the key kept with-source difficulty but sat at +40.4. This draws options from related-but-distinct stimuli in the SAME scenario family, aiming at the corridor between the two measured endpoints.
servingConstraint: Items sharing a family MUST NOT be served in the same test. They share an option set verbatim; a student seeing two of them could pair them. This is the production analogue of the mirror-pair pilot's finding that pairs are spottable.
stoppingRule: If the no-source margin does not fall at least 10 points below the +40.4 baseline, the mutation-recipe hypothesis is wrong. Stop; do not author a round 2. The previous pilot's round 2 bought 0.4 points.
